summary: Read recent Unity Console entries for debugging.
whenToUse: You need recent errors, warnings, or info messages from the Unity Editor.
You want a quick read-only debugging step before trying a more invasive tool.
whenNotToUse: You need to change project state instead of inspecting it.
You need visual scene context rather than text logs.

argumentGuidance.name: maxEntries
argumentGuidance.guidance: Start with a small value such as 5 or 10 to avoid noisy output.

argumentGuidance.name: includeStackTrace
argumentGuidance.guidance: Use false for quick scans and true when you need the exact call path.

argumentGuidance.name: logTypes
argumentGuidance.guidance: Limit the result with a comma-separated subset such as error,warning when narrowing a problem.

examples.title: Read the latest warnings and errors

summary: Compile and run a C# editor script inside Unity.
whenToUse: You need to automate an editor task that no focused tool already covers.
You need to inspect or mutate Unity state with custom C# logic.
whenNotToUse: A dedicated Unity MCP tool already covers the task more safely.
You only need logs or screenshots.

argumentGuidance.name: Code
argumentGuidance.guidance: Wrap the script in an internal CommandScript class that implements IRunCommand.

argumentGuidance.name: Title
argumentGuidance.guidance: Use a short label when you want the execution to be easier to identify in logs.

examples.title: Create a cube through the golden template
examples.command: unity-ai-cli call Unity_RunCommand --json-args '{"Code":"using UnityEngine; using UnityEditor; internal class CommandScript : IRunCommand { public void Execute(ExecutionResult result) { GameObject cube = GameObject.CreatePrimitive(PrimitiveType.Cube); result.RegisterObjectCreation(cube); result.Log(\"Created {0}\", cube); } }","Title":"Create cube"}'

sideEffects: Can modify scenes, assets, packages, and project settings.
Bad scripts can fail compilation or make destructive editor changes.

summary: Render an image from a specific camera or the current Scene View.
whenToUse: You need to inspect what a particular camera sees.
You need image context that text tools cannot provide.
whenNotToUse: A text description of the scene is enough.
You only need the Unity Editor UI rather than camera output.

argumentGuidance.name: cameraInstanceID
argumentGuidance.guidance: Pass the camera GameObject instance ID when you want a specific camera rather than the current Scene View.

summary: Capture the current Unity Editor UI as an image.
whenToUse: You need visual context from the editor itself, such as docked windows or scene view layout.
You want a screenshot without writing a custom editor script.
whenNotToUse: You only need a specific camera output.
Logs or tool output already explain the problem.

summary: Capture the current Scene View from four angles in a 2x2 grid.
whenToUse: You need broad 3D spatial context for a scene layout review.
One screenshot is not enough to understand scene structure.
whenNotToUse: A single Scene View or camera capture is enough.

examples.title: Capture a 3D scene from multiple angles

summary: List available generation models for Unity asset generation tools.
whenToUse: You need a valid model ID before generating or editing an asset.
You want to inspect which generation backends are currently available.
whenNotToUse: You already know the exact model ID to use.
You are not using asset generation.

argumentGuidance.name: includeAllModels
argumentGuidance.guidance: Set true when you need the full model inventory rather than the curated default list.

examples.title: List the currently available generation models

summary: Generate or edit a Unity asset through the asset generation backend.
whenToUse: You want to generate a new sprite, image, cubemap, material, sound, or mesh.
You want to edit an existing generated asset with a prompt.
whenNotToUse: You are only exploring which models are available.
The task can be completed with a normal editor script or import workflow.

argumentGuidance.name: command
argumentGuidance.guidance: This selects the generation action and is always required.

argumentGuidance.name: modelId
argumentGuidance.guidance: Get a valid model ID from Unity_AssetGeneration_GetModels before calling this tool.

argumentGuidance.name: savePath
argumentGuidance.guidance: Use a project-relative asset path when creating a new generated asset.

argumentGuidance.name: targetAssetPath
argumentGuidance.guidance: Provide the existing asset path when the command edits or augments an asset.

argumentGuidance.name: waitForCompletion
argumentGuidance.guidance: Set true when the caller should wait for a finished generation job.

examples.title: Generate a sprite asset
examples.command: unity-ai-cli call Unity_AssetGeneration_GenerateAsset --json-args '{"command":"GenerateSprite","modelId":"<model-id>","prompt":"A stylized wooden crate icon","savePath":"Assets/Generated/crate.png","waitForCompletion":true}'

sideEffects: Generation can be expensive and may depend on external generation services.
